html:
The capture and destruction of Jerusalem by the army of Nebuchadnezzar II of Babylon in 586 BCE (some scholars prefer 587). It ended the kingdom of Judah and began the Babylonian exile.

Judah's king Zedekiah, put on the throne by Babylon, rebelled with hopes of help from Egypt. After a long siege the walls were breached. The Babylonians burned Solomon's Temple, the royal palace and the city's houses. According to the Bible, Zedekiah saw his sons killed and was then blinded and led in chains to Babylon. Much of the upper class was deported, joining those taken in 597 BCE.

The fall ended the line of kings from David that had ruled since the kingdom of David and Solomon. Yet exile reshaped Judaism. Without a temple, the exiles held together around their scriptures, the Sabbath and their laws, and much of the Hebrew Bible took its final form in this period. Psalm 137 begins "By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down and wept". The exile ended about fifty years later with the Return to Zion under Persian rule.
sum: The capture and destruction of Jerusalem by the army of Nebuchadnezzar II of Babylon in 586 BCE (some scholars prefer 587). It ended the kingdom of Judah and began the Babylonian exile.
